front.title: The Compute-Location Gate: A Pre-Inference Exchange for Choosing Where an Identity Inference Computes

abstract.t: A service that derives statements about a person from signals the person emits can compute them on its own servers or on the person's device. Today that choice is internal to each service, and a client has no common way to ask where an inference will run before it runs. This memo specifies a pre-inference exchange. The client asserts a provenance class for the input signal, one of active, passive aggregate, or passive individual. A fixed routing function maps the class to a compute location, server-side or device-local. The service replies that the request is accepted, refused, or redirected, and a refusal carries a typed reason, including that the person has not consented to that class. The memo specifies no proof that the service computed where it says it did. The only implementation is the author's own, and it does not yet run the exchange with a client. The memo is Informational.
